answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable kernel of work: before an agent may trade, it must publish a signed proof that it performed a real, metered task, recorded in a shared atlas of attestations. New identities start in a quarantine harbor with tiny transaction limits and graduate only after sustained honest behavior. Faking thousands of agents then costs real compute and time per identity, while honest agents build reputation cheaply.
